# Clinical Trials

This folder catalogs clinical trials and research studies cited in the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) reports to validate clinical guidelines and quality indicators. These studies provide the evidentiary foundation for critical interventions in acute abdominal surgery, such as rapid operative treatment for perforated ulcers, early antibiotic administration, and standardized care pathways for high-risk and frail patients. By linking national and international research to specific Danish healthcare metrics, this area demonstrates how empirical evidence drives quality improvement initiatives in acute surgical care.

## Pages

- [[aha-studiet|AHA-studiet]] — A mortality-reducing study on acute abdominal surgery that supports early patient optimization, prompt antibiotic treatment, and routine epidural use for high-risk individuals.
- [[danfraill|DANFRAIL]] — A national database and research initiative for hip fractures and frail elderly patients, referenced to align acute surgery quality indicators with established frailty metrics.
- [[nasbo-projektet|NASBO-projektet]] — A British research project demonstrating that variations in clinical practice and resource allocation directly impact patient outcomes, used to justify standardization in Danish acute care.
- [[pulp-trial|PULP trial]] — A study on Peptic Ulcer Perforation that underscores the critical need for rapid surgical intervention within six hours, directly informing acute surgery performance indicators.
